title: Take a drawer off its slides by pressing two opposite-sense release levers while pulling, then set it down
instruction: Take the drawer fully out of its slides and set it down on the table in front of the cabinet, then let go.
context: Taking a kitchen or desk drawer off its ball-bearing slides is a routine job when cleaning, painting or fixing a cabinet. Each slide has its own spring release lever, and the two levers work in opposite senses: one is pushed up, the other pushed down. Each lifts a latch dog clear of a fixed block in its channel, so both must be held while the drawer is drawn forward past the block. Working one lever leaves the other dog against its block and the drawer jams. Once past the blocks the drawer is free of the cabinet except for resting on its rails; the robot carries it off the rails, lowers it onto the table and lets go.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; table top z 0.7475. (1) Drawer bay (fixed): plywood, sRGB (0.70, 0.55, 0.35), 8 kg, 300 x 316 x 200 mm (front face x 0.38, y -0.158 to 0.158, z 0 to 0.200 above the table) on an 85 mm plinth. Per side a steel slide channel, sRGB (0.62, 0.63, 0.66), from 20 mm in front of the bay face to its back: an 8 mm web (|y| 137.2 to 145.4 mm, z 107.5 to 155.5 mm) and a bottom rail (|y| 121.5 to 145.4 mm, z 107.5 to 114.5 mm). Latch blocks 10 mm long, 126 to 136 mm behind the bay face, |y| 133.0 to 137.2 mm: left 5.5 mm tall on the rail (z 114.5 to 120.0 mm), right hanging from the web (z 145.0 to 155.5 mm). (2) Drawer, a free body with no joint to the bay: 12 mm plywood, sRGB (0.86, 0.76, 0.56), 1.2 kg, 280 x 240 mm, walls 65 mm, inset front, 6 mm bottom, friction 0.5; two steel inner slide members 230 x 12.7 x 35 mm at |y| 120 to 132.7 mm, z 115 to 150 mm above the table, resting 0.5 mm above the rail tops. It stands pulled out 129 mm (front face at x 0.251), bottom 100 mm above the table. No part hangs below the bottom plane. Brackets on the walls: left, a 55 x 21.5 x 5 mm flange on the wall top (drawer z 60 to 65 mm); right, a 55 x 21.5 x 5 mm flange at drawer z 34 to 39 mm with a 3.8 mm slot at y -137 to -133 mm. (3) Left release lever (red, ABS, 20 g): a 35 x 21.5 x 3 mm tab at drawer z 31 to 34 mm, y 123.5 to 145 mm, pushed UP 6 mm against a 1.2 N/mm spring (5.4 N at the 4.5 mm that counts as pressed, 7.2 N at full travel), on a 3.8 mm latch bar (y 133 to 136.8 mm, z 28 to 36 mm) along the inner member ending in a 12 mm dog that hangs to z 16.5 mm. Tab underside to flange top 34 mm. (4) Right release lever (blue, 20 g): a tab of the same size at z 65 to 68 mm pushed DOWN 6 mm against the same spring, on a 3.8 mm stem through the flange slot and a latch bar at z 28.5 to 37.5 mm ending in a dog that stands up to z 48.5 mm. Flange underside to tab top 34 mm. (5) Latch: at rest each dog overlaps its block by 3.5 mm; at 4.5 mm of travel it clears by 1 mm; the dog faces meet the blocks at 130 mm of extension. With one lever held and 30 N pull the drawer must not pass; with both held it passes at under 5 N. Past the blocks nothing holds the drawer but the rails (it rests on them until its rear is 290 mm out) and the grippers.
scoring: Final state only, at the end of the episode (success must hold 1 s); nothing earlier in the run is held against it. 0: the drawer is not off both slides (any part less than 10 mm in front of the bay face). 0.25: off both slides, but not flat on the table and at rest for 1 s (held in the air, tilted or still moving). 0.5: off both slides, all four bottom corners within 4 mm of the table top, at rest (under 5 mm/s) for 1 s, a gripper not yet clear. 1.0: also both grippers 30 mm or more from every part of the drawer and under 10 mm/s for 1 s (release gate). The score does not read the levers: a dog that is not lifted stops against its block. Real-trial measurement: a side video at 30 fps and a tape on the bench top. Off the slides: the drawer rear reads at least 10 mm in front of the bay face. Flat: a 4 mm feeler blade does not pass under any bottom corner. At rest: no tape movement over 30 frames. Clear: a 30 mm spacer card passed around each gripper and the drawer. Lever rig check (not scoring): each latch bar carries a printed 6 mm scale and a 1.5 mm band covered at rest and visible only at 4.5 to 6.0 mm of travel; the tab-to-flange pad span is 34 mm at rest and 29.5 mm or less when the band shows (28 mm at full travel).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lift the drawer onto the rails from above (inner members on the rail tops, dogs in front of their blocks), slide it to the 129 mm stop, let both levers spring back to rest, and check the 5.4 N lever force at 4.5 mm with a spring scale. Re-mark the 6 mm bar scales if they have worn.
fidelity: Full-size drawer, plywood, steel channels, springs, dogs and levers. The drawer is a free rigid body resting on rails: detaching it and setting it on the table are done by the arms and gravity, with no joint or brake standing in for the slide. The simulator keeps the intermediate slide members rigid and fixed to the bay, modelled as a rail 20 mm proud of the bay face. A real drawer would not close back through the lever tabs, so the rig is reset by lowering the drawer onto the rails from above.
